clue.text: Send watch to be wound back

indicators.note: winding a watch back suggests turning the word for it round to read from the other end

parts.note: a watch is a timer

explanation.surface: An instruction to post a watch off so its hands can be wound back.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send, especially money or a matter to another body.

clue.text: Fraudster, one playing tennis you might say?

definitions.meaning: a criminal running a dishonest business

definitions.text: one playing tennis you might say?
definitions.meaning: a whimsical coinage for someone who wields a tennis racket, with -eer as in auctioneer

explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a criminal scheme; the second reading jokingly builds a racket user.

clue.text: Mushroom added with first of lentils

parts.note: more means additional, added on

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of lentils

explanation.surface: A recipe where mushrooms are added with a few lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: A morel is an edible fungus with a honeycombed cap.

clue.text: Other plays with me, one's proven

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters of other and me are toyed with into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone else plays with me, and one of us proves the stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a statement that has been demonstrated by proof is so called.

clue.text: Marine species lookin' to catch you, ultimately

indicators.note: to catch means to hold something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lookin' is a dropped-g form of looking, i.e. searchin'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Someone casually searching the sea for a creature, looking for you in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'lookin'' licenses the clipped form SEARCHIN, which takes in U, the last letter of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny echinoderm living on the seabed, a marine animal.

clue.text: Crossword writer in sun at the end of the day?

definitions.text: sun at the end of the day?
definitions.meaning: the sun at dusk is something that sets, so fancifully one that sets

explanation.definitionFit: A compiler of puzzles bears this title; the sun going down at evening is whimsically the thing setting.

clue.text: Dog on telly, bitter

parts.note: aired means broadcast, shown on television
bitter is a British type of ale

explanation.surface: A dog shown on television looks sour.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a hoppy British beer, so it gives ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Bacon poor as her sausage sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches means the words hold the answer between them, enclosed within

explanation.surface: Bacon is a poor relation, as her sausage sandwiches prove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food, but it signals the letters held inside 'poor as her sausage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers are thin slices of bacon, so the plural noun stands for bacon.

clue.text: Awkward problem, sexy King Edward?

parts.note: hot means sexy or attractive
King Edward is a popular British variety of potato

explanation.surface: Asking whether a monarch was alluring and also a tricky issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks like a monarch but is a British potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an idiom for a controversial issue nobody wants to handle.

clue.text: Group has nothing to break your fall

parts.note: no means none, nothing
a safety net catches a falling acrobat

explanation.surface: A circus troupe working without any safety net.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine musicians.

clue.text: Woodworker adds fish to log

indicators.note: adds signals that one piece is simply joined to the next in sequence

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to log something is to enter it in a record

explanation.surface: A woodworker puts fish on a log fire, or records fish in a logbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a craftsman who makes and repairs wooden structures.

clue.text: Day at home that's smooth and silky

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A lazy day at home spent feeling relaxed and comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, satin describes a glossy finish or texture like the fabric, hence smooth and silky.

clue.text: Stretch where angler repositioned line, finally

indicators.note: repositioned tells us the letters of angler are moved into a new order
finally takes only the closing letter of the word line

explanation.surface: A fisherman shifts position and casts his line one last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repositioned' rearranges ANGLER into ENLARG, and 'finally' adds E, the end of 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge is to make bigger, much as stretching extends something.

clue.text: Tedious novel ceases to exist

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of Tedious appear in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A boring book that eventually stops being read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the book being described, but it is the anagram signal on 'Tedious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A species or custom that dies out becomes extinct, no longer existing at all.

clue.text: Inexplicable thing being in game as every other character sent off

indicators.note: sending off alternate letters, starting with the first, leaves the second, fourth, sixth and so on of being in game as

explanation.surface: A puzzling football match where half the players are sent off by the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent off' suggests a sporting dismissal; here it removes the odd letters of 'being in game as', leaving the even ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or puzzle that cannot easily be explained.

clue.text: Minder put off being foolish

indicators.note: off means wrong or bad, so the letters of minder put are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carer being put off would be unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means lacking care or good sense, unwise.

clue.text: Terms in list are endless in magazine

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the other one

parts.note: a glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper

indicators.note: endless removes the final letter of the word are

explanation.surface: Pointing out that words listed in a magazine run on without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts ARE to AR, which goes into GLOSSY.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of specialist words with their meanings.

clue.text: Number in the sixties, a short way back

definitions.meaning: a song from the 1960s, here the Beatles track of 1965
adverbially, not long ago in the recent past

explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles recorded a famous ballad of this title in 1965, and the word means the day before today.

clue.text: Plane is not dismantled for scrap

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft

indicators.note: dismantled means taken apart, so the letters of is not are rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A plane is not taken apart for scrap metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to discard or abandon something, as cargo thrown overboard.

clue.text: Journalist on carrier

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a porter carries luggage

explanation.surface: A journalist reporting from an aircraft carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes news.

clue.text: A minor revolutionary leading a nation

indicators.note: leading means coming before, so the shuffled letters precede the last word
revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the letters of a minor are shuffled

explanation.surface: A young rebel heading a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: A burden describing some clues

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden one must endure

explanation.surface: A solver remarks that some clues are a real burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Clues are split into those running horizontally and those running down, so half of them are labelled this way.

clue.text: Outfit a huge hit

definitions.meaning: British slang for clothes and gear
to strike very hard, as a verb meaning to land a heavy blow

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the word covers clothing and belongings, and as a verb it means to hit hard.

clue.text: Attitude about right for thread

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a stand is a stance or attitude on an issue

explanation.surface: A change of position towards fairness about some thread of argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a single fibre or thread.

clue.text: Top police force take a nosedive

parts.note: plum means top or best, as in a plum job
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: The best police force's reputation suddenly crashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply and quickly, like a plane in a nosedive.

clue.text: Model in picture, so pumped up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
in tells us the letters sit within the words picture so pumped

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder model in a photo looking muscly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pumped' looks part of the scene but supplies a letter; 'in' takes RESOP from 'pictuRE SO Pumped' and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser sits for an artist or photographer, as a model does.

clue.text: After opening of trading, currency in difficulty

indicators.note: after says the currency comes following the single letter
opening of takes just the first letter of trading

parts.note: the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: When the markets open, a currency gets into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble is a state of difficulty or distress.

clue.text: Something elasticated in mind

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment with elastic

explanation.surface: Wondering about something with elastic in it, deliberately vague.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ of thought, so it stands for the mind.

clue.text: Authoritarian back on ship

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: Stern is both a severe adjective and the noun for a boat's aft section.

clue.text: Right in the main?

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea, so right in the main means the right side on a ship

explanation.surface: Seems to mean correct for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly', but 'the main' is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing forward on a vessel, the right-hand side carries this nautical name, opposite port.

clue.text: Interred, a rogue learned new skills

indicators.note: rogue means behaving wildly, so the letters of interred and a are scrambled

explanation.surface: A villain buried and then dug up again has acquired fresh abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone retrained has been taught again for a different job or task.

clue.text: Fruity edges of raspberry?

wordplay.reading: R at one end and Y at the other

parts.note: the outer letters of raspberry are an R and a Y, so spelling out that pair, letter, link word, letter, gives the entry

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the rims of a raspberry taste particularly fruity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruity' suggests flavour, but here it is the slang sense of lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruity in British slang can mean sexually suggestive or lustful, a synonym.
